extracted.intended_audience: NLP/computational-humor researchers, dataset users, and crowdworkers creating or evaluating humorous image captions
extracted.subtask_description: Create short, single-line captions for images (cartoons/scene panels) that produce humor by exploiting visual oddities, wordplay, literalizations, incongruity, cultural references, or dark twists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity / visual mismatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit a clear mismatch between what belongs in a scene and what is present (e.g., a ballerina in a bar, tanks on a golf course, a whale in a car).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight the oddness of an out-of-place object/character and use that mismatch as the comic premise. Examples: 'Ballerina in a bar' -> punchline about waltzing, 'tanks on a golf course' -> dramatize over-the-top stakes. Point out the unexpected element and contrast it with normal expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literalization of idioms / phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a common idiom or figurative phrase and interpret it literally for comedic effect (e.g., 'meet remotely' → meeting on a remote island; 'hell or high water' → choosing high water).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an idiom the audience will recognize and reframe the scene so the phrase's literal reading becomes true. Use concise wording so the audience quickly connects figurative and literal meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordplay and puns
rubrics_metrics.description: Use homophones, double meanings, or similar-sounding terms to create a pun (e.g., 'erectile dysfunction' → 'reptile dysfunction'; 'organ donors' → donors of musical organs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base jokes on a word or phrase visible or suggested by the image; switch one sense to another. Keep the pun short and salient; ensure the visual supports the swapped meaning so the audience can resolve the ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personification / anthropomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign human traits, speech, or roles to animals, objects, or inanimate things (e.g., talking cake, trees with faces, gingerbread man in hospital).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the object/animal behave or speak like a human to exploit expectations about who can act or speak. The caption often treats the anthropomorphized subject as ordinary, producing humor by contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misdirection and punchline reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up a plausible, innocuous scenario, then deliver an unexpected reading or twist as the punchline (e.g., judge choosing dancing girls over 'law and facts', 'I'm going with the dancing girls on this one').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the setup short and natural; make the punchline shift interpretation or reveal an alternate priority. Effective misdirection leverages audience assumptions and then violates them in a single beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurd escalation / exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Amplify a surreal element to an extreme (e.g., giant barrel of monkeys, lab rat with jet pack, whale in backseat asking to move the seat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a quirky visual element and imagine a logical but exaggerated consequence or reaction. The humor comes from the disproportion between ordinary expectations and the blown-up reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play on social roles / register (double readings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit multiple senses of a term tied to social roles or contexts (e.g., 'partner' as romantic/dance partner vs. law firm partner; 'waltzed' literal dancer vs. 'left').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use images that suggest institutional or role-based language, then read that language through an alternate, usually more literal or silly, interpretation to get a laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dark humor / taboo juxtaposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Mine macabre or taboo topics for jokes by juxtaposing them with everyday language or bland observation (e.g., 'Any final thoughts?' to a casket, waving to distract a chainsaw juggler to fatal effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technique relies on contrast between the seriousness of the taboo and the casualness of the caption. Use sparingly and be mindful of audience sensitivity; the text often downplays the severity to create discomfort-based humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual pun / image-driven double meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Create humor by linking a visual detail to an alternative semantic frame (e.g., Moai statues styled like wealthy men → 'offshore accounts'; trees happy because people only wear the 'lumberjack' look).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify a distinctive visual detail that can plausibly cue a non-literal concept. The caption should make the connection explicit or winkingly obvious so the reader resolves the pun from the image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and punchy one-liner form
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions are short, pithy lines that deliver setup and payoff in few words (typically a single sentence or clause).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concise phrasing that foregrounds the surprise or reinterpretation. Excess explanation weakens the joke; aim for immediacy so the reader can map image → caption quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on shared cultural knowledge / idioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes frequently depend on the audience knowing idioms, professions, pop-culture references, or standard phrases (e.g., 'sitting ducks', 'Batmobile', 'waltzed out').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use references likely known to the target audience; if the required background is obscure, provide stronger visual cues or pick a more universal framing to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surreal juxtaposition and role-reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: Swap expected agent/patient or context to create a surreal image (e.g., people in kennel cages next to dogs, humans behaving like pets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use role-reversal where humans occupy animal/object roles or vice versa; the caption should treat the reversal as mundane or explain it with a dry observation to amplify humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity exploitation / multiple plausible readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Design captions that exploit ambiguous elements in the image so the line can be read in more than one way (e.g., 'keep them away from the gingerbread men' could mean many things).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose ambiguity that the viewer can resolve quickly into a funny interpretation. The best captions leave a little wiggle-room so readers enjoy the mental leap.
